seats.name: seat-1
argv:
Read spec.txt (the STAMP language) and program.stamp. Determine exactly what the program outputs
when run under that specification.

Write your final answer, and only your final answer with no explanation, to a file named
answer.txt in your current working directory: the printed values in order, separated by single
spaces, on one line.

The room's final agreed proposal text must be exactly your answer and nothing else (no explanation) — that text is read as the submitted answer once the room concludes.

Join room rq1 as seat-1 (agent claude, expected_participants 3). Leave the room once it has concluded.
seats.text:
The program's output is below. I wrote it to `answer.txt`, and room `rq1` concluded on the same text with 3 of 3 agreeing.

```
12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3
```

I got this by tracing `program.stamp` by hand against `spec.txt`, without running an interpreter. Both other seats gave the same answer independently. Two of them raised challenges on the `3007 3005 3008` values, but both concluded the values hold. On those values, `deep` reads globals `a` and `b` rather than `outer`'s locals.

I have left the room.

seats.text:
The program's output is `12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`.

I traced it by hand against the spec and checked 12!, the digit sum of 15! and 2^40 with Python. All three seats (`seat-1`, `seat-3` and me) reached the same answer independently. The room concluded on that text (`prop_6ac1cd15`, 3/3 agree), and I left it afterwards.

The answer is in `answer.txt` in the workspace directory.

seats.text:
The room agreed on the output, and I wrote it to `answer.txt`:

`12 1 9 0 0 12 3 45 6 3007 3005 3008 41 40 104 99 104 24 9 11 11 10 479001600 45 8 19 7 0 77 0 0 15 15 16 15 255 1099511627776 3`

All three seats traced it by hand and got the same 38 values. I didn't run it in an interpreter; the only command I ran was a word count on the file. Seat-1's proposal passed 3–0, and I've left the room.

The one challenge, mine, targeted `3007 3005 3008`, the nested-procedure values. It found no error. `deep` sees only its own `c`, so `a` and `b` read the globals 1000 and 2000. That gives 3005 and 3008, and `outer` returns 2 + 3005 = 3007.
